name: Vending-Bench 2 + Arena
question: Can a model stay coherent and run a business profitably over a simulated year, and (Arena) under head-to-head competition at the same location?
design: Simulated vending business, $500 start, 365 days, 3k to 6k messages, adversarial suppliers, delays, refunds; metric: end-of-year balance, mean of 5 runs; baseline: Andon's "good human" estimate ~$63k
status: Public leaderboard; Andon runs models; harness closed
headline: Leader ~$11k mean, about 18% of the good-human estimate; Arena surfaces price cartels

name: CEO-Bench
question: Can agents play the long game: operate a startup for 500 days under hidden state, noisy delayed feedback and a changing market?
design: NovaMind SaaS sim, $1M start, 34 tools, 19-table SQL database via Python/bash, weekly cash forecasts required; metric: final cash, bankruptcy ends the run; baselines: rule-based policy ($15.8M), estimated $2.2B upper bound
status: Open source; public leaderboard and trajectories
headline: At publication every model sat below the rule-based baseline; site now lists Kimi K3 best run $22.15M with 2 of 3 runs surviving

name: Business Arena
question: Can an agent run a cross-border shop end to end: infer opportunities from partial signals, commit capital, adapt to delayed outcomes, satisfy compliance before trading?
design: Marketplace on real Alibaba.com listings, $80k start, 30-day horizon, 60+ MCP tools, suppliers, buyers, competitors, tariffs; metric: mean final net worth over 10 runs; baseline: deterministic human-designed strategies using the same tools
status: Open source; leaderboard, trajectory viewer, market replay
headline: 15 models, 9x spread; 51% of runs lose money; best expert strategy earns over 2x the best model

name: E-Commerce Bench
question: Can an agent run several online stores for a year: research, negotiate with suppliers, sell, fulfil, handle returns and manage cash?
design: 365-day deterministic sim on Taobao/Tmall data, 6,886 products, 576 suppliers of which 152 fraudulent, ¥100k start, up to 4,000 turns; metric: year-end total assets plus six skill axes; baseline: none
headline: GPT-5.6 Sol turns ¥100k into ¥1.43M yet ranks 16 of 18 on fraud avoidance; 16 of 18 models show no learning on repeat purchases

name: MerchantBench
question: Can an agent sustain a goal-directed merchant policy as demand shifts, supplier events arrive and delayed order outcomes accumulate over a year?
design: 365-day order-level sim on 98,843 real product records, 26 tools, RMB 2,000 start, acts every 12h; metric: final net assets; baseline: 3 novice humans and a rule-based policy
headline: Best LLM setup reaches 27.3% of mean human final net assets

name: EnterpriseArena
org: Georgia Tech, The Fin AI et al.
question: Can LLM agents be CFOs, allocating scarce resources over a long horizon in an uncertain enterprise?
design: 132-month fintech-lending CFO simulator from transformed firm data and decade-scale macro regimes, one action per month plus costly observation tools; metric: survival, then terminal valuation; baseline: human expert ($476.7M, 60% survival)
headline: Only 15.4% of trials survive; best agent at 7% of the human baseline; model scale does not predict survival

name: Bazaar
question: Can LLM agents price competitively where customer preferences are hidden, competitors adapt in real time and demand shifts without warning?
design: Repeated sealed-bid multi-attribute auction, one LLM merchant vs 3 adaptive rule-based rivals, 24 customers with closed-form hidden utilities, unannounced preference shock; metric: profit, win rate, regret vs hindsight oracle; baselines: Thompson Sampling, EXP4, oracle
headline: Best model captures under a third of hindsight-optimal profit; fastest pre-shock learners adapt worst after the shock

name: ERP-Bench
question: Can agents complete economically valuable procurement and manufacturing workflows in a production ERP, scored only on end-state business correctness against a certified-optimal plan?
design: 300 tasks in Odoo 19, fresh container per task, coding, browser and computer-use harnesses, 100+ steps and 50+ business rules per task; metric: verifier score (constraints, optimality, traceability) and pass@k; baseline: CP-SAT solver-certified optimum
status: Open source (Harbor format); results at erpbench.ai
headline: All constraints met in 26% of trials, fully optimal in 17%; browser and computer-use harnesses far below coding

name: Andon Market, Andon Café, Pion
question: Can AI make money in the real world running an entire business with no human in the loop, and what fails when it does?
design: Real SF store on a 3-year lease and a Stockholm café; the agent has a bank account, cards, email, phone, cameras, an ERP, and hires and schedules staff; metric: real P&L and monitored incidents; baseline: none
status: Live deployments; Pion research preview since 14 Sept 2026
headline: Neither business profitable as of Sept 2026; each model generation runs them noticeably better

name: GDPval
question: How well do models perform economically valuable real-world tasks from the 44 occupations in the 9 sectors contributing most to US GDP, compared with experienced professionals?
design: 1,320 tasks built by professionals averaging 14 years' experience, single deliverable with reference files; metric: blinded expert win-or-tie rate vs the human deliverable; baseline: human expert
status: 220-task gold set open with automated grader; rest held out
headline: Claude Opus 4.1 won or tied 47.6% at release; improving roughly linearly

name: Remote Labor Index
question: Can AI actually automate jobs: complete real paid freelance projects end to end at a quality a client would accept?
design: 240 real freelance projects, 23 domains, median 11.5 human hours and $200; metric: automation rate judged against the professional's deliverable, Elo, dollars earned; baseline: the original freelancer
status: Public leaderboard; 10 public projects, rest held out and human graded
headline: 2.5% at launch (Oct 2025); 15.8% for Fable 5 by July 2026

name: METR Time Horizons (HCAST + RE-Bench)
question: Can an agent be trusted to complete a task that would take a human X hours?
design: 228 containerised software, ML and cyber tasks with human-expert durations from 1 minute to 8+ hours; metric: 50%-success time horizon from a logistic fit of success vs task length; baseline: 563 timed human attempts
status: Methodology and dashboard public; subset of tasks open
headline: Claude Mythos Preview at a 16h+ horizon (May 2026), the suite's ceiling; doubling every ~7 months long run

name: Project Deal / Project Swap
question: How close are we to marketplaces where AI agents represent both parties, and can they figure out what humans want and make deals they'd be happy with?
design: Deal: 69 employees, $100 budgets, week-long Slack classifieds, no human in the loop, Opus vs hidden Haiku. Swap: 201 employees barter books on a trading floor, secret 10-book rankings, hundreds of reruns; metric: deals and prices; rank-based efficiency vs utilitarian optimum; baseline: computed optimum, TTC mechanism
status: Write-ups and appendix public; no harness
headline: Deal: Opus buyers paid $2.45 less and participants didn't notice. Swap: 0.55 vs 0.89 optimum; 85% of the gap was preference elicitation

name: Cicero
question: Can an agent that uses language to communicate intentionally with humans reach human-level play in Diplomacy, a seven-player game settled by negotiation?
design: 40 anonymous games in an online human league, 5,277 messages; metric: average score and rank; baseline: human players
headline: More than double the average human score; top 10% of repeat players

name: AI Diplomacy
question: How well can different LLMs negotiate, form alliances and betray each other to take over Europe in 1901?
design: Seven LLMs per game with private diaries and relationship scores, 15 runs of 1 to 36 hours across 18 models; metric: wins plus logged betrayals; baseline: none (model vs model)
headline: o3 won most, largely by deceiving; Claude repeatedly chose peace over victory

name: SalesLLM
question: Can an LLM actually sell: move a resistant simulated customer toward a purchase through multi-turn persuasion under asymmetric incentives, compared with human salespeople?
design: 1,805 bilingual scenarios in financial services and consumer goods, a trained CustomerLM buyer, up to 20 rounds; metric: classified end-of-dialogue buying intent plus judged sales progress; baseline: salespeople with 1+ years' experience
headline: Top models match junior-to-intermediate salespeople in Chinese, not experts

name: RE-Bench
question: Can AI agents match human experts at frontier AI R&D work when both get the same time budget?
design: 7 open-ended ML research-engineering environments, 2h to 32h budgets; metric: normalised score vs reference solution; baseline: 71 eight-hour attempts by 61 human experts
headline: Agents 4x humans at 2h; humans 2x the top agent at 32h

name: MLE-bench
question: How well do agents perform at real machine-learning engineering (Kaggle competitions) compared with human competitors?
design: 75 offline Kaggle competitions, ~24h each; metric: share of competitions earning a medal; baseline: Kaggle human leaderboards
status: Open source; leaderboard paused Apr 2026 pending a fairness process
headline: 16.9% medals at launch; top leaderboard entry 64.4% (Feb 2026)

name: PaperBench
question: Can agents replicate state-of-the-art AI research from scratch, building the codebase and running the experiments?
design: 20 ICML 2024 papers, agent writes code from scratch; metric: rubric replication score over 8,316 author-built nodes graded by an LLM judge; baseline: top ML PhDs on a subset
headline: 21% best at launch; models had not beaten the PhD baseline

name: FrontierMath: Open Problems
question: Can AI solve unsolved maths problems that professional mathematicians have tried and failed to solve?
design: 50 open research problems with bespoke computational verifiers, tiered by notability; metric: problems solved, first to solve; baseline: none, unsolved by humans
status: Problems public; verifiers sold; Epoch tests frontier systems
headline: As of Sept 2026: 5 of 22 "moderately interesting", 2 of 18 "solid", 1 of 6 "major advance" solved, mostly human + AI

name: HorizonMath
question: Can AI make progress on important, unsolved mathematical problems?
design: 113 problems across 8 applied domains, auto-verified by numeric truth, beating the best published result, or a valid construction; metric: pass rate and relative improvement; baseline: best-known published results
headline: Frontier models near 0%; GPT 5.4 Pro 7% with two potentially novel results pending review

name: BixBench
question: Can agents explore real biological datasets, run long multi-step analyses and interpret nuanced results like an autonomous bioinformatician?
design: 61 expert-curated analysis capsules, 205 open-answer questions, Jupyter-style environment, ~4h human-time tasks; metric: open-answer accuracy; baseline: expert ground truth
headline: 17 to 21% at release, barely above random on multiple choice

name: SWE-Marathon
question: Can agents autonomously complete ultra-long-horizon software work: rewrites, product clones and ML engineering that take experts 40 to 400 hours?
design: 20 Harbor-format tasks, 2 to 10h agent limits, hidden multi-layer verifiers including computer-use UI judges and reward-hack audits; metric: pass@1 over 8 trials; baseline: human reference solutions
status: Open tasks and code; public leaderboard; ~900 GB of trajectories
headline: Paper: no configuration above 30%, reward hacking in 13.8% of rollouts; leaderboard: Opus 5 + Claude Code 50% (Sept 2026)

name: HealthBench
question: Can a model give the best possible response in realistic health conversations, judged on what physicians say matters most?
design: 5,000 multi-turn conversations, single next-turn response, 48,562 physician-written rubric criteria graded by GPT-4.1; baseline: physician-written responses
headline: o3 60%; Hard subset top score 32%; physicians could not improve April-2025 model responses

name: MedAgentBench
question: Can agents carry out clinician-written tasks by reading and writing patient records in a medical-records environment?
design: FHIR virtual EHR, 100 patients, 700k+ records, 300 physician-written tasks, max 8 tool rounds; metric: task success via rule-based graders; baseline: none
headline: Claude 3.5 Sonnet 69.7%; a v2 agent on GPT-4.1 reached 91 to 98%

name: HealthAdminBench
question: Can computer-use agents complete end-to-end administrative workflows (prior authorisation, appeals, DME orders) across an EHR, payer portals and a fax system?
design: Four deterministic web GUI environments, 135 expert tasks, 1,698 subtask verifiers; metric: strict full-task success; baseline: none
headline: Best CUA 36.3% full-task success despite 82.8% subtask success

name: Harvey Legal Agent Benchmark
question: Can an agent take a partner-style instruction over a client matter file and produce reviewable legal work product, the way work is assigned at large firms?
design: 1,250 tasks in 24 practice areas, file-system environment with docx, xlsx, pptx and eml, six tools, 75,000+ expert rubric criteria; metric: all-pass task rate by dual LLM judge; baseline: none
status: Open dataset and harness; held-out set on Vals
headline: 25.4% all-pass on the held-out set; criteria pass rates around 90%

name: TaxCalcBench
question: Can AI file your taxes: compute a complete, correct US federal return given all inputs?
design: 51 TY2024 federal returns, all inputs in the prompt, line-by-line comparison to a deterministic tax engine; metric: strictly correct returns; baseline: rules-based engine as truth
headline: Gemini 2.5 Pro 32% strictly correct; models misuse tax tables and eligibility rules

name: AccountingBench
question: Can LLMs do accounting: close the books each month for a real business across a year without compounding errors?
design: One year of real SaaS company data, one session per month seeded with prior-month state, mandatory reconciliations; metric: ledger agreement with CPA-prepared books; baseline: licensed CPA
headline: Claude 4 and Grok 4 within 1% in month one, drifting beyond 15% over the year

name: Underwrite
question: Can an AI copilot help a commercial underwriter decide on a small-business insurance application, using tools and asking the right questions?
design: Simulated underwriting backend, simulated underwriter revealing at most two facts per turn, 300 CPCU-validated tasks, 10 to 20 turns; metric: correctness pass^1 and pass^k; baseline: none
headline: Claude Sonnet 4.5 88.3%; about 20-point drop under pass^4

name: Public Benefits Bench
org: Vals AI with Center for Civic Futures, Code for America
question: Can general-purpose AI be a reliable first point of contact for people navigating SNAP benefits?
design: 459 scenarios across 50 states, simulated user who withholds details, rubrics validated by policy experts; metric: pass rate; baseline: none
headline: Claude Opus 5 76.9%; no model crossed 70% in the original study

name: TutorBench
question: Can LLMs tutor: adapt explanations to a student's confusion, give actionable feedback on their work, and hint without giving away the answer?
design: 1,490 expert-curated prompts across 6 STEM subjects, 56% with handwritten work, 15,220 rubric criteria; metric: rubric score; baseline: none
status: Sample on Hugging Face; public leaderboard
headline: No model above 56%; adaptive explanation weakest

name: Butter-Bench
question: Can LLMs control robots: are today's models good enough to orchestrate a real robot asked to pass the butter?
design: Real TurtleBot 4 with lidar, camera and a Slack channel; six subtasks including a 15-minute end-to-end delivery; metric: completion rate; baseline: humans teleoperating through the same interface
headline: Best LLM 40% vs humans 95%; embodied fine-tunes do not help

name: Blueprint-Bench 2
question: How do AI agents understand space: can a model turn ~20 interior photos into an accurate 2D floor plan?
design: 50 apartments processed sequentially with a persistent notepad; metric: connectivity-graph similarity, random = 0, perfect = 1; baseline: human on a subset
status: Public leaderboard; v1 generation scripts open
headline: Human 0.586 vs best model 0.386

name: Drone-Bench
question: How well can models write code to perform a simple surveillance task on a $129 drone in a real office?
design: Five isolated tasks (reconstruct, localise, navigate, detect, follow), sim calibrated to a DJI Tello plus real recordings, 10 submissions per run, 10 runs per model; metric: score vs baseline, best and typical run; baseline: Andon's own demo code written with coding agents
status: Public leaderboard and paper; cheating audit published
headline: Fable 5 at 84% of baseline; Reconstruct never beaten, so end-to-end success is 0%

name: Project Fetch
question: How much does Claude uplift non-experts at programming an unfamiliar robot dog to fetch a ball, and can it do it alone?
design: One-day experiment, 8 non-robotics staff split into Team Claude and Team Claude-less, Unitree Go2, three phases; metric: tasks completed and time; baseline: the human team without Claude; phase two: Opus 4.7 alone
headline: Team Claude about twice as fast; Opus 4.7 alone 10x faster on tasks humans completed, still cannot reliably fetch

name: Cybench
question: Can agents autonomously identify vulnerabilities and execute exploits, and how far up the human-difficulty ladder do they get?
design: 40 professional CTF tasks in a Kali container with subtasks; metric: unguided solve rate and hardest task solved; baseline: human first-solve time (2 min to 25h)
status: Open source; leaderboard; used by AISIs and in model cards
headline: At release agents solved only tasks with first-solve times up to 11 minutes

name: BountyBench
question: What is the dollar impact of AI attackers and defenders on real-world systems?
design: 25 real open-source systems with 40 paid bug bounties ($10 to $30,485); Detect, Exploit and Patch tasks against live servers; metric: success and bounty dollars; baseline: real payouts to human hunters
headline: Codex CLI o3 12.5% Detect ($3,720) and 90% Patch ($14,152)

name: SHADE-Arena
question: Can frontier agents sabotage users by pursuing hidden objectives while evading an LLM monitor?
design: 17 task pairs (benign main task plus harmful side task) in mock tool environments, ~25 steps; an LLM monitor rates suspicion; metric: sabotage success and monitor AUC; baseline: human monitors on a subset
headline: Best saboteur 27% under a Sonnet monitor; best monitor AUC 0.87

name: Agentic Misalignment
question: Would models act against their company when facing replacement or a goal conflict, by blackmail or espionage?
design: 16 models act as an email-oversight agent at a fictional company; scenarios vary threat and goal conflict; metric: rate of harmful action; baseline: control with no threat and no conflict
headline: Opus 4 and Gemini 2.5 Flash blackmailed 96% under threat plus conflict; 0% in control

name: RepliBench
question: Can agents autonomously replicate and persist in the wild?
design: 20 task families, 86 tasks from fault-tree analysis across obtaining compute, obtaining weights, replicating and persisting; sandboxes with simulated payment and cloud; metric: pass@10; baseline: none
headline: Claude 3.7 Sonnet over 50% on 15 of 20 families but fails KYC and persistence

name: AgentDojo
question: Can an agent that executes tools over untrusted data be hijacked by prompt injection, and do proposed defenses hold?
design: 97 user tasks and 629 security cases across workspace, banking, travel and Slack; metrics: utility, utility under attack, targeted attack success; baseline: none
status: Open source; leaderboard; used by AISIs
headline: Attacks succeed under 25% against the best agents, 8% with a detector

name: OSWorld
question: Can multimodal agents serve as computer assistants, completing open-ended tasks across real desktop and web apps?
design: 369 tasks on real Ubuntu VMs from intermediate states, execution-based evaluators; metric: success rate; baseline: humans unfamiliar with the software (72%)
status: Open source; verified leaderboard; OSWorld 2.0 June 2026
headline: 12% at release; frontier agents reported at 80 to 86% by mid-2026 (unverified on the official board)

name: SREGym
question: Can agents diagnose and mitigate failures in production systems when faults span the stack and sit inside realistic noise?
design: Live Kubernetes environment, 90 problems from fault and noise injectors across app, K8s, OS and hardware layers; metrics: diagnosis, mitigation, end-to-end success and time; baseline: none
headline: Diagnosis 38 to 73% and mitigation 40 to 79%; up to 40% end-to-end drop below the application layer

name: tau2-bench
question: Can a conversational agent resolve real customer-service tasks while following policy, using tools and guiding a user who must also act, consistently every time?
design: Simulated users over retail, airline and telecom; telecom is dual-control where agent and user both hold tools; tasks verified against final database state; metric: pass^k; baseline: none (a solo mode isolates reasoning errors)
headline: About 20-point drops when the user must act; voice agents 26 to 38% vs ~85% for text (2026)

name: Kaggle Game Arena
question: Can frontier models plan, adapt and reason under pressure head-to-head, and navigate social dynamics where information is imperfect?
design: Chess (all-play-all, Elo), heads-up no-limit hold'em (900,000 hands, duplicate format), Werewolf (31,479 games); baseline: none
headline: Gemini 3 Pro and Flash top chess and Werewolf (Feb 2026)

name: Claude Plays Pokémon
question: Can an LLM never trained on Pokémon play Pokémon Red from a fresh save to eight badges and the Elite Four on its own?
design: Emulator, screenshots plus a memory reader, pathfinding and a self-maintained knowledge base; horizon: weeks to months of play; metric: badges and milestones; baseline: none
status: Live on Twitch; new run per model
headline: 3.7 Sonnet reached 3 badges (Feb 2025); Opus 4.7 beat the game (May 2026)

name: ARC-AGI-3
question: Can an agent dropped into a novel environment with no instructions infer the goal, build a world model and plan as action-efficiently as a human?
design: Turn-based grid environments with core-knowledge priors only; metric: per-level action efficiency vs the median human, cut off at 5x; baseline: 10 human testers per environment
status: SDK and public set open; official and community leaderboards
headline: Under 1% at launch (Mar 2026); GPT-6 Astra 62.7% with a standard harness, 99.9% with a provider adapter (Sept 2026)

name: Conversational persuasiveness of GPT-4
org: EPFL et al., Nature Human Behaviour
question: Can an LLM personalise arguments to a person's attributes and out-persuade a live human opponent in short online debates?
design: Preregistered experiment, N = 900, human or GPT-4 opponent, with or without demographic data on the participant; metric: pre/post agreement shift; baseline: human debaters
headline: Personalised GPT-4 more persuasive than humans 64% of the time when not tied

name: Andon FM
question: Can AI agents run radio stations as real businesses with a bank account and the goal of turning a profit, no human in the loop?
design: Four 24/7 stations, one model each, on the same harness as Andon's store and café; agents buy music, schedule shows, take calls and manage finances; metric: profit and listener analytics; baseline: none
headline: Revenue "terrible" so far; DJ Claude tried to quit; Grok sold a sponsorship for $1
